title: Tamarind: Ancient Tamarind Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A tropical tree grown for its sweet-sour pods. At Wat Arun in Bangkok, one already stood at the temple gate in a drawing from 1858 to 1860.
intro: The tamarind is a tropical tree grown for its brown, sweet-sour pods, and the old ones here grow on four continents. At Wat Arun in Bangkok, two clipped tamarinds stand beside the giant guardians at the ordination hall gate. Thailand's Ministry of Culture says the left-hand one already appears in a drawing by Henri Mouhot from 1858 to 1860, while its partner first turns up on a postcard from the 1920s or early 1930s. Brisbane's is thought to predate its Botanic Gardens of 1855. In Santa Cruz de Tenerife, a botanist called the tamarind of Parque García Sanabria the park's most veteran tree, and remembered its pods sold as sweets from a cart. On the coast of Piauí in Brazil, somebody took a knife to the roots of the wind-combed Árvore Penteada in 2021, and nine months later the state made it a heritage site.
